_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals

pit_profile.why: The Southern Company: 'The traditional electric operating companies – Alabama Power, Georgia Power, and Mississippi Power – are each operating public utility companies providing electric service to retail customers in three Southeastern states in addition to wholesale customers in the Southeast. Southern Company Gas is an energy services holding company whose primary business is the distribution of natural gas in four states – Illinois, Georgia, Virginia, and Tennessee – through the natural gas distribution utilities.'; among its risk factors, 'Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial federal, state, and local governmental regulation, including with respect to rates.', 'The operating results of the Registrants are affected by weather conditions and may fluctuate on a seasonal basis.' and 'The Southern Company system's costs of compliance with environmental laws and satisfying related AROs are significant.' (its own FY2020 10-K); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12): the company owns coal and lignite reserves and its CO2 risk factor puts the theme on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Southern Company

theme_watch.reason: Live: Southern Company's own FY2020 10-K says 'Alabama Power owns coal reserves near its Plant Gorgas site and uses their output in its generating plants. Mississippi Power owns a lignite mine and equipment that were intended to provide fuel for the Kemper IGCC. Mississippi Power also has mineral reserves located around the Kemper County energy facility.' and, among its risk factors, 'The Southern Company system may be exposed to regulatory and financial risks related to the impact of GHG legislation, regulation, and emission reduction goals.' The stock trades at 21.0x FY21E — a premium. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ENERGY_TRANSITION) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing decarbonisation of Southern Company's coal reserves and the units they supply specifically.

BEAR.desc: EPS -34.9%/yr (worst year FY11-FY20 ex-FY17, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +15.5%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY17 median

BULL.desc: EPS +15.5%/yr (FY11-FY20 ex-FY17 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +16.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY11-FY20 ex-FY17); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: SO (retrospective, 2021-06-25) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.70x (72.4% downside to Bear $17 / +26.8% upside to Bull $78) | Adj composite 3.30 vs market 3.77: gap -0.47 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +50% above the EPP floor $41 (14x FY21E $2.93) | Conservative 2-yr case: +6.7% total (+3.4%/yr) | At 21.0x FY21E the 15% hurdle price $81 sits above the BULL case; retail kWh sales +1.8% in Q1 2021, forward revenues +17.8% (no Q2 2021 revenue guide, Q1 2021 revenue as reported); the energy transition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
